doc.title: Attention Is All You Need (demo fixture)

chunks.text: The Transformer is a sequence transduction model based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show the model is superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train.

Recurrent models factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and output, which precludes parallelization within a training example. Attention mechanisms allow dependencies to be modeled regardless of their distance in the sequence.

Both the encoder and the decoder are a stack of N=6 identical layers. Each encoder layer has two sub-layers: a multi-head self-attention mechanism and a position-wise fully connected feed-forward network, each wrapped in a residual connection followed by layer normalization. The decoder adds a third sub-layer that attends over the encoder output, and its self-attention is masked so a position cannot see later positions.

Attention computes the dot product of a query with all keys, divides each result by the square root of d_k, and applies a softmax to obtain weights on the values. The scaling matters because for large d_k the dot products grow large in magnitude, pushing the softmax into regions where gradients are extremely small.

Instead of a single attention function with d_model-dimensional keys, values and queries, the model linearly projects them h times with different learned projections and attends in parallel. The base model uses h=8 parallel attention heads. For each head the dimensions are d_k = d_v = d_model/h = 64.

Each layer contains a fully connected feed-forward network applied to each position separately: two linear transformations with a ReLU in between. The input and output dimensionality is d_model=512 and the inner layer has dimensionality d_ff=2048.

Because the model has no recurrence and no convolution, information about token order is injected by adding positional encodings to the input embeddings. These are sine and cosine functions of different frequencies.

Self-attention is compared with recurrent and convolutional layers on three criteria: computational complexity per layer, the amount of computation that can be parallelized, and the path length between long-range dependencies. A self-attention layer connects all positions with a constant number of sequentially executed operations.

The models were trained on the WMT 2014 English-German dataset of about 4.5 million sentence pairs and on the larger WMT 2014 English-French dataset. Base models were trained for 100,000 steps, about 12 hours, on one machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs. The big models were trained for 300,000 steps, about 3.5 days.

Training used the Adam optimizer with beta1=0.9, beta2=0.98 and epsilon=1e-9. The learning rate increases linearly for the first 4000 warmup steps and then decays proportionally to the inverse square root of the step number. Regularization includes residual dropout of 0.1 and label smoothing of 0.1.

The big Transformer reaches 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over the previous best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU. On English-to-French it achieves a single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8.
